source: D154 P8 (45n) — the AI-engineering route's BUILDS, drafted by the agent for the owner's review. A build is proven the D169 way: a public link (repository or write-up) added as proof on the skill, which makes it 'built'. Nothing here is served until its status is 'approved'.

builds.title: A leak-free baseline
builds.brief: Take a public tabular dataset, split it into training, validation and test sets the right way, and train one simple model. Show its metric on the test set once, at the end.
steps: Pick a public dataset with a clear target (a churn, fraud or price dataset).
Split before you look: training, validation, test. If rows share a person or a time, split by person or by time.
Train a baseline (logistic regression or a small tree) and choose its settings on the validation set only.
Report the test metric once, with the metric you chose and why it fits the problem.
Write down one leak you checked for and how you checked.
builds.show: A repository with the notebook or script, and a README that names the split, the metric and the leak check.

builds.title: Serve a model and watch it drift
builds.brief: Put the baseline behind a small HTTP endpoint, log what it is asked, and add one drift check that compares this week's inputs with the training data.
steps: Wrap the model in a small service (FastAPI or similar) with one predict endpoint.
Log each request's inputs and the prediction (no personal data).
Add a drift check: compare one input's distribution this week with training (a population stability index or a simple histogram distance).
Say what you would do when the check fires.
builds.show: A repository that runs with one command, and a README showing a request, its log line and the drift check's output.

builds.title: Retrieval over your own documents, with an evaluation
builds.brief: Build a small question-answering tool over a set of documents you are allowed to use, and measure it: a fixed set of questions with expected answers, scored before and after one change.
steps: Choose 20–50 documents you may use (your notes, a project's public docs under an open licence).
Split them into chunks, embed them, and retrieve the top few for a question.
Ask a model to answer only from what was retrieved, and to say when the answer isn't there.
Write 20 questions with the expected answer and the document it comes from.
Score retrieval (was the right document retrieved?) and the answer (right, wrong, or 'not there'), change one thing (chunk size, number retrieved), and score again.
builds.show: A repository with the evaluation set, both scores, and one paragraph on what the change did.

builds.title: An agent with two tools and a limit
builds.brief: Give a model two tools (for example a calculator and a search over your documents), return structured output, and stop it safely: a step limit, a cost limit and a refusal it can give.
steps: Define two tools with clear input schemas.
Ask for structured output (JSON with a schema) and reject anything that does not parse.
Add a step limit and a cost limit, and log every tool call.
Write five tasks it should finish and two it should refuse, and record what it did.
builds.show: A repository with the tool definitions, the logs of the seven tasks and what each one cost.

builds.title: A support assistant, end to end
builds.brief: Combine the retrieval build and the agent build into one assistant for a made-up product's help pages, with an evaluation, a cost per answer, and a guardrail for questions it must hand to a person.
steps: Write or gather 30 help pages for a made-up product.
Answer from retrieval; hand off billing and account questions to a person instead of answering.
Measure accuracy on 30 questions, the hand-off rate, and the cost and time per answer.
Write a one-page design note: what you would change before real users saw it.
builds.show: A repository and the one-page design note with the measured numbers.
